items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The two brothers Papo, who were two young boys then, took us out in the city to sightseeing.

ctx.x: The first time I ever saw my name in lights was the night we played in Le Mans, which was the 19th of October, after the Salle Pleyel concert. I was surprised when I arrived at the Cinema Rex in that city and saw "Bill Coleman and his orchestra " in big red lights on the marquis.

The next time I saw "Bill Coleman and his orchestra" in big lights was when we did a concert in Barcelona, Spain, the 19th of November. It was a coincidence that it was just one month after Le Mans, and it was a pleasant sight for me to see. And I was thrilled to have had the opportunity to be the first American jazz man to do a concert in Spain since Benny Carter had done one there in 1936. It was the first time I had set foot in that country, and we were treated like Kings. The two brothers Papo, who were two…

The tour also taken us to Belgium for three concerts and 8 in Switzerland, which was something extremely rare for an orchestra to do in that country. But there are plenty of jazz fans in Switzerland, and I was quite well known there. And I'm certain that I'm the only American musician that ever done concerts in 43 cities in France with a group.
